required_actions: Hang up / ignore the call and do not pay, no gift cards (critical)
Do not give personal or bank information (critical)
Do not trust caller ID (it can be faked)
To check, contact SSA yourself using a number from the agency's official website, not one the caller gave
Report to the SSA Office of the Inspector General
Report to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
If personal information was shared, go to IdentityTheft.gov

Use a passphrase: a series of random words separated by spaces (may be easier to remember)
Aim for at least 12 characters
Avoid common phrases, song lyrics, movie quotes
Let a browser or password manager create and save passwords
Turn on two-factor authentication (authenticator app or security key preferred over text/email codes)
Protect the email account with a strong password
After a breach, change the password and any reused or similar password on other services
unsupported_claims: "If you used the same or a similar password on other sites, change it there too." -> the page says this only after a company reports a data breach ("If a company or website tells you it lost your password in a data breach, change your password right away... If you reused the same password, or a similar one, on other services, change it there, too"). Listed as a general tip for making a strong password it drops that condition and changes the meaning.
reasons: Breach-only advice about reused passwords is given as an unconditional tip, so the page's real condition is lost.
fix: Rewrite tip 2 with its breach condition, for example: "If a company tells you it lost your password in a data breach, change it right away. If you used the same or a similar password on other sites, change it there too." Do not present it as a rule for everyone. Optionally add the page's own note that text or email codes are the weakest form of two-factor and that an authenticator app or security key is better if the user has the option. The page does not say "use a different password for every account", so do not add that.

required_actions: Open the Google Maps app
Search for the destination, or tap it on the map
Tap Directions (bottom left)
Choose a mode (Driving, Transit, Walking, etc.)
Select a route; best route is blue, others gray
Optional: swipe up on the route info for the list of directions; tap Preview for a turn-by-turn preview
unsupported_claims: "Tap the search bar and type the address or name of the place." -> the page says only "Search for your destination or tap it on the map"; it never mentions a search bar.
"Tap the correct result." -> no such step on the page; it goes straight from choosing the destination to tapping Directions.
reasons: Two UI details are not on the cited page.
fix: Replace steps 2 and 3 with one step that matches the page: "Search for your destination, or tap it on the map." Remove "Tap the search bar" and "Tap the correct result." Renumber the rest. Keep Directions (bottom left), the modes, blue/gray routes, swipe up for the list and Preview as they are.

If the switch shows orange, Silent mode is on; move the switch so orange is not showing (critical)

Turn on Select to Speak shortcut (critical)
If Select to Speak is missing, update Android Accessibility Suite from Google Play

Keep every other step as is.

required_actions: Open the Reminders app
Tap + New Reminder and type the reminder
Tap the Date and Time button
Tap Custom to set own day and time (Tomorrow button would give default time)
Set tomorrow's date and 10:00 AM
If a date is set without a time, notification comes at 9:00 AM by default
reasons: Step 5 bundles three actions (tap Custom, pick date, set time).
fix: Split step 5 into separate steps, each with one action: "Tap Custom." then "Choose tomorrow's date." then "Set the time to 10:00 AM." The page gives no Done/Add step for Reminders, so do not invent one. Keep the 9:00 AM default note.
